I congratulate the Prime Minister for announcing a unilateral 
ceasefire during the holy month of Ramzan. Later on it was extended 
twice. The gesture of the Prime Minister was hailed by the world 
leaders and by the people of Jammu and Kashmir. This has forced 
Pakistan's chief executive Pervez Musharraf to tone down his anti-
India stand. Politically, the Centre  must quickly decide on allowing 
APHC leaders to travel to Pakistan to hold talks with the militant 
leaders there. We should find permanent peace in J&K. not a 
temporary one. 
We agree that there is an improv ement in the situation in the 
North-East. This region requires a faster socio-economic development. 
The agreement with the NSCN for three years is going to expire. I 
hope the Government has worked out'on extending the same for a 
further period. With the opening of road  from the North-East Region to 
Myanmar, the trade development will witness a faster growth. The 
mindless killing of innocent people and non-Assamese by the ULFA in 
that region is very unfortunate, I hope the Government is taking action 
to put down the activities of this  militant outfit. The Government can 
think of declaring a unilateral ceasefire in the North-East Region as 
has been done in J&K. 
We must agree that the NDA Government is committed to 
secularism. The scale of communal and caste violence has come 
down despite efforts from across the border to create communal 
trouble in India. Tamil Nadu Government is also committed to 
promoting communal harmony. We have decided to institute an award 
in the name of Coimbatore Kottai Amir who worked for religious 
harmony and lost his life at the hands of religious fundamentalists. The 
Government should remain vigil ant against communal and extremist 
organisations. I thank the Government for increasing financial 
assistance for modernisation of State Police Forces. I hope this 
amount will be increased in the near future also. 
We are not happy with the recommendations of the Eleventh 
Finance Commission. Tamil Nadu has suffered a huge financial loss 
on account of the recommendations of the Eleventh Finance 
Commission. Tamil Nadu Government  has requested that the States' 
share of the gross tax revenues of the Centre be fixed at 40 per cent. 
As against this request, the Eleventh Finance Commission 
recommended the devolution of only 29.5 per cent of the net tax 
revenues. Moreover, the Commission has given greater weightage to 
the backward States while fixing norms for sharing these revenues;  
well-performing  States  like  Tamil  Nadu  have  been  adversely

affected.  As a result, the revenue toss that Tamil Nadu will suffer in 
the five years from the year 2000 is estimated to be Rs.4711 crores. 
The States affected by the recommendations of the Finance 
Commission had submitted a memorandum to the Prime Minister on 
21-8-2000 requesting that this was unacceptable and this inequitable 
situation be rectified. We had also  suggested that an Incentive Fund 
for extending grants to well-performing States should be created. In its 
supplementary Report, the Eleventh Finance Commission has 
recommended a total incentive grant of Rs.5,304 crores for all the 
States for the next five years. The fa ct is that our total share of this 
grant for five years would be only Rs.402 crores. This amounts to 
severely punishing the welt-performing States like Tamil Nadu. The 
overall deficit in the interim Budget for the year 2001-2002 has been 
estimated at Rs.99§ crores. This leve l of deficit would not have arisen 
had the Eleventh Finance Commission been fair to us. Therefore, as 
one of the measures for raising re sources, I request the Central 
Government to increase the incentive grant to the State Governments. 
No doubt, India is among the ten fastest growing economies 
in the world, The Government has set an ambitious target of 9 per 
cent annual growth for the next ten years, to double our per capita 
income and remove poverty. To sustain a growth rate of 10 per cent, 
an investment rate of 35 per cent is required. The rate of domestic 
savings has steadily dropped. The do mestic savings provide over 98 
per cent of the nation's total inve stment funds. The Government must 
give more and more incentives for domestic savings. Reforms in the 
power sector are crucial for achieving a to per cent growth rate. 
The Tamil Nadu Government has also requested the Central 
Government to clear the proposal for an international airport at 
Chennai. The land has been acquired. The Project report has been 
prepared and submitted to the Civil Aviation Ministry. The Tamil Nadu 
Government has proposed to operate it under the BOT scheme. I 
urge upon the Central Government to clear the.proposal at the 
earliest. More and more FDI is coming into Tamil Nadu. If we have to 
achieve the ambitious growth rate of 10 per cent, then, the proposal 
for an international airport at Chennai should be cleared immediately.

foodgrains production of 209 million tonnes last year. Our buffer- stock 
has crossed an all-time-high of 40 million tonnes. But we do have the 
storage problem. I think the Government is exporting the surplus 
foodgrains. But it should export the foodgrains at not Jess than the 
price fixed for the PDS. The minimum support price should be 
announced before the harvesting season. In spite of announcing the 
minimum support price, the farm ers are not getting remunerative 
prices for their produce. The middlemen are cheating our farmers. The 
Governmental agencies should ensure  purchase of the produce from 
the farmers at the minimum support price. I am glad that our 
Government has increased the import duties on agricultural 
commodities in order to protect our farmers. The scope of the National 
Crop Insurance Scheme should be widened. To ensure that the 
farmers get a good price for their paddy, the Government of Tamil 
Nadu is implementing a parallel procurement system for the current 
Samba season. This is the only State which provides Rs.40 per quintal

price fixed by the Central Government. Tamil Nadu Government is 
spending Rs.1.700 crores towards food subsidy alone.

Rs.3.50 per kg to all sections of the public, without any distinction 
between those living below the poverty line or above the poverty line. I 
would request the Central Government to increase the allocation of 
funds to Tamil Nadu.

Central Government for giving approval for upgradation of roads,
